program_overview.title: Problem Solving for Teens
program_overview.tagline: The thinking behind the code: logic, data structures and algorithms taught until a teenager can face an unseen problem and actually solve it.
program_overview.description:
The hardest, most valuable thing in programming is not syntax, it is looking at a problem you have never seen and finding your way to a solution. This live online course builds exactly that in a teenager, step by step and at a teen pace: logic and programming foundations first, conditionals, loops, functions, the core structures (arrays, strings, hash maps, stacks, queues, linked lists, recursion), then the real data structures and algorithms, trees, heaps, graphs, sorting and searching, algorithm-design paradigms, and finally dynamic programming and the problem-solving techniques that separate confident solvers from stuck ones. Every topic is taught through problems, not lectures, and the emphasis is always on the pattern, so a new problem is solvable, not a memorized answer. A finale month builds a problem-solving portfolio and sits a final exam.

The pace is honest and teen-friendly: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus three to five hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets after every class, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.

Patterns over memorization: the skill is solving unseen problems
A real teen pace: depth without the burnout of an adult bootcamp
The foundation serious students build on: olympiads, contests and later interviews
An honest 10-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What does this problem-solving course for teens cover?
faqs.answer: Logic and programming foundations first (conditionals, loops, functions, arrays, strings, hash maps, stacks, queues, linked lists, recursion), then core data structures and algorithms (trees, heaps, graphs, sorting, searching, algorithm design), then dynamic programming and problem-solving techniques with counting and geometry basics. Everything is taught through problems, focusing on transferable patterns. A finale month builds a problem-solving portfolio and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn problem solving properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Does my teenager need coding experience to start?
faqs.answer: No. The course begins with programming logic from scratch and builds up. What matters is curiosity and a willingness to sit with a hard problem, which is exactly the habit the course trains. Any language works; we most often use Python because it keeps the focus on the thinking.

faqs.question: Is this the same as your competitive programming course?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference is deliberate. This teens course builds the foundation, logic, data structures, algorithms and problem-solving patterns at a teen pace. Our competitive programming course is the intense, contest-focused next step (advanced techniques, speed, olympiad and ICPC preparation), and our DSA course is the interview-focused one. Teens who finish this and want more are perfectly placed for either.
